newsitem.title: FRANCE: European Union nations lodge Belarus protest.
newsitem.headline: European Union nations lodge Belarus protest.

text.p: France, Germany, Britain and Italy have protested to Belarus authorities at what they called the illegal nature of a referendum called by President Alexander Lukashenko next Sunday in a bid to to increase his powers.
French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters on Tuesday that ambassadors of the four European Union countries had delivered the protest in Minsk.

"We have expressed to Belarus authorities our concern at the illegal nature of this referendum following last week's events and the sacking of the president of the electoral commission," Rummelhardt said.

Lukashenko has called the vote to amend the constitution and tighten his grip on rival institutions. He earlier fired the head of the independent election commission and ignored rulings by the constitutional court.

"France reasserts its desire that the Minsk authorities respect the essential values on which democracy is based," Rummelhardt said. "France hopes that all parties will reach a solution through dialogue and respect of the constitutional order."

Prime Minister Mikhail Chigir, who had remained loyal to Lukashenko during months of political paralysis, resigned on Monday. Lukashenko named deputy prime minister Sergei Ling as acting premier. Labour minister Alexander Sosnov also resigned.

In Strasbourg, the parliamentary assembly of the Council of Europe said Lukashenko's moves could jeopardise prospects for Belarus membership of the 40-member body which promotes democracy and human rights.

"We fear that the constitutional crisis shaking Belarus may jeopardise that country's chances of joining the Council of Europe," said a statement by assembly speaker Leni Fischer and the heads of the assembly's political groups.
The assembly urged Lukashenko to heed the decision of the constitutional council which said on November 4 that the referendum should have no legal force.
Deputies have been occupying parliament around the clock since Friday to protest at Lukashenko's ideas.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin called on Tuesday for compromise and common sense in neighbouring Belarus and said he was worried about the rise in tension there, the Kremlin said.
